cells.tense: The strength is here today and the level stays true while the work is done.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask someone close how it's really going, then stay past the first answer — through the pause, into what they didn't start to say — and hold it for them.
cells.core:
You can hold what a person is carrying and still see what's true without one swallowing the other, and that is no small thing where feelings run high. People bring you their messes. You take the weight, you stay level, and nothing tips. Whatever gets built on that stays standing, which is what lasting things are built on.

The invitation is closer listening rather than more care. Ask someone how it's going and stay in the answer past the polite part; the pause is where the real thing lives. Fixing isn't asked of you here. Two people near each other, each still whole and neither merged — that is fair weight kept well, and yours to practise while the ground is firm.
cells.sheetLine: Hold the level, then stay long enough to hear what someone means.
cells.verb: holding things up and keeping them whole
cells.place: where fair weight is kept level

cells.tense: The holding will keep going past what it can bear, and the tally will arrive first.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Before the next call about someone close, set down in two columns what it costs them and what it gives. Read both. Then decide, once.
cells.core:
Where you hold things up, the grip has gone quiet and tight. The next load is already being weighed before it lands — steady or not, will this hold — and the scale runs while the plates are still warm. The strength is real. It has just been drafted into counting, and what was holding has started to press. Walls go up against storms that pass by, and the ones inside feel the walls.

What brings the level back is a fair look at the true thing, not more force. Before the next call about someone close, put the cost to them and the gain side by side on paper. Read both columns, then decide. The judgment you already trust knows the way; it only needs the real weight on it, not the imagined one.

cells.tense: The pushing was spent before this hour, and what remains stands at a threshold already crossed.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Mark one carried load as finished, set it down, then take a single step on the unfinished one.
cells.core:
The muscle that holds things up is tired in a particular way — too little resisting, too little pushing. You answer fast, you defer fast, and the fair call arrives a day late, so what waits for you is the tidy-up after a thing has already gone. The strength is still in you. It has been standing at a shut phase long enough that the next stretch looks like somebody else's work.

What pulls the current back is finishing, not forcing. Take one load carried that has already closed — the conversation, the project, the season — and mark it done. Set it down. Then take one step on what is still unfinished, and only that step. What is finished can be released; what is not gets the effort. The account does not have to feel settled to get cleared.

cells.tense: Fair weight is being kept level here and the keeping has never been claimed.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin again this week, on purpose, one small act that keeps things fair for someone. No explanation, no tally. Just begin it.
cells.core:
You hold things up and keep them level, and by your own account it amounts to nothing. Making the fair call, absorbing the awkward part, keeping the room standing — when anyone asks, the answer is that you don't do much. That answer is wrong. The strength has been operating with you missing from the sentence.

This reconnects to something smaller and earlier than what you've been doing. Begin again this week, deliberately, one act of fairness you already perform for someone — no explanation, no tally. Starting it on purpose puts you back in the sentence. The shine comes later; the starting comes first, and it is allowed to be about the starting alone.

attempts.check: The kernel names a balanced face for the signature (holding without forcing) but does not state that the person has lost or is losing that capacity in any particular relationship, handle, or room — so any core that names a specific burden, person, or history is unsupported. The reader could reasonably say 'my steadiness isn't crushing anyone right now, and I don't recognise that tightness as mine.' The asks survive being wrong because each is one visible act that teaches something even if the read misses. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any line about what has happened between them and someone else, or any line praising the read itself.
